title: Reap fire and forget threads with pthread_join
summary: Join the threads that sleep used to wait for, take the sum back as the return value, then stop joining inside the create loop.

turns.user: checksum thing sometimes prints 3 lines instead of 4 on big files. valgrind also says possibly lost in pthread_create. and i want the total back in the caller, not printf in each thread

assistant.body: Great catch! checksum starts the threads and then just sleeps for a second, so any thread that takes longer is still running when it returns, and when main exits its output goes with it. A thread that is neither joined nor detached keeps its stack and other resources even after it finishes, which is the possibly lost valgrind reports. pthread_join waits for the thread to end and hands back whatever the thread function returned, so each thread returns a malloc'd sum. jobs only has to live while the threads run, so it moves into the function.

turns.user: numbers are right now. but its 4x slower. top shows 100% cpu, not 400

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was wrong. It called pthread_join right after pthread_create inside the same loop, so the second thread did not start until the first one had finished. In other words, it was serial code that happened to use threads. Starting and reaping now happen in two loops. If pthread_create fails partway, every thread already started is still joined before returning.
